correctness.rationale: The proof reduces the centered equilateral length to a sum of coordinate squared norms on a hexagon. Strict convexity characterizes exactly the six equality columns. An explicit nearest-vertex rounding lemma proves both squared-distance and row-energy L1 bounds, from which integer balancing yields the 4/5 and 4/7 deficits and near-equality 6/5 threshold; block concatenations prove all claimed feasible bounds. Exact symbolic identities and 30,000 rational column tests were replayed. The finite test suite does not replace the all-dimensional inequalities.

evidence: Ionin (2015) gives unrestricted squared side (8/3)d in the side-two cube when 3 divides d, versus centered 2d here.

broader_coverage.reasoning: A stronger unrestricted-domain maximum cannot imply the smaller centered-domain optimum, much less its full equality orbit, cardinality, residue gaps and distance stability, without a missing hypothesis-specific theorem. The full-dimensional/volume theorems concern different invariants. Their general mathematical techniques may transfer, but their statements do not dominate this claim.

originality.rationale: Closest accessible direct prior work is Ionin 2015 on the same geometric containment but without fixed centroid; it yields a strictly larger unrestricted maximum and not the fixed-center equality count, residue-gap lower bounds or metric stability. Wenzel concerns full-dimensional cube-vertex simplices, Ambrus–Gárgyán central-section volumes, and the indexed OEIS counts vertex triangles. Those exact comparisons and residual risks are detailed below.
residual_risks: Older or non-indexed fixed-centroid cube containment research may provide an equivalent inequality, orbit classification or near-equality theorem.

The exact optimum in the two nonsaturated residue classes is open here; only a gap interval is established.

value.rationale: The fixed-center restriction is geometrically natural for central cube sections and changes the optimal scale and equality set relative to unconstrained inscribed triangles. The result completely characterizes saturation and its exponentially many equality configurations, proves uniform positive losses exactly in the other two residue classes, and controls Euclidean distance of every sufficiently near-saturating triangle to the discrete extremal orbit. This yields nontrivial structural and quantitative conclusions in every dimension without pretending to solve the remaining exact residue optima.
